text:
sophie: Heads-up — I ran the new int4-reranker against core_holdout and saw a consistent NDCG@10 drop (~6%) on short queries (<20 tokens). Full run attached.
alex: thanks — can you paste the eval command and the exact model tag you used?
sophie: model: ranky-7b-int4-v2, dataset: core_holdout_v3, cmd: `python eval.py --model ranky-7b-int4-v2 --dataset core_holdout_v3 --k 10 --slice short_queries --seed 42`
sam: 6% is pretty large for short queries. Does the delta show up across MRR and P@1 or just NDCG?
sophie: NDCG@10 -6%, MRR ~ -2%, P@1 ~ -3%, tails barely changed. The histogram shows a bunch of small queries with top1 flips.
maria: did you normalize query/doc whitespace or run with the same tokenizer/byte-level settings as baseline?
sophie: yes same preprocessing pipeline. I double-checked tokenization; sample pair: `q: "install zsh mac"` baseline ranks doc A, int4 ranks doc B.
alex: can you dump logits/topk probs for a few flipped examples? I'm curious whether quant noise is changing score gaps or if there's a calibration shift.
sophie: attaching a small table in the next message — but quick sample: baseline gap=1.8, int4 gap=0.2 on one sample (score compression)
sam: that feels like calibration/scale compression. We should run a calibration curve sweep (temperature/rescale) and see if a global affine transform recovers ordering.
maria: also try per-slice rescale: short_queries vs long_queries. If short queries use fewer tokens, KV cache and quantization alignment might affect norms.
sophie: agreed. I'll run rescale grid: scale in [0.9,1.0,1.1,1.2] and bias in [-0.2,-0.1,0,0.1] and report NDCG@10.
deploy-bot: CI test for eval harness finished — 72 tests passed, 1 flaky skipped :white_check_mark:
alex: FYI I've seen int4 kernels produce slightly lower variance in logits because of clipping. Could be a side-effect of the quantization LUT we used.
sam: if rescaling helps, we can bake a post-quant calibration step for short-query workloads. But we also should check whether this is dataset-specific (core_holdout_v3) or shows up on sampled production traces.
sophie: running the rescale sweep now. Quick interim: scale=1.1, bias=0.0 recovered ~3.5% of the loss (NDCG now -2.5% vs baseline). Will run full table.
maria: please also run the same eval with a float16 variant (ranky-7b-fp16) on the same harness to rule out non-quant regressions.
sophie: queued fp16 run — baseline check coming up.
alex: can we instrument the eval harness to output per-query score variance across model seeds? Might help see if quant increases instability.
sam: good idea. Add `--emit-score-trace` option that writes per-candidate scores into traces.json, then we can compute within-query variance.
sophie: done — rerunning with emit. Also adding a small script to compute per-query z-score shifts.

# example command
```
python eval.py \
  --model ranky-7b-int4-v2 \
  --dataset core_holdout_v3 \
  --k 10 \
  --slice short_queries \
  --seed 42 \
  --emit-score-trace traces_short.json
```

sophie: initial trace for 10 flipped cases shows mean score compression factor ~0.62 vs baseline and std reduced.
maria: interesting — reduced std + compressed mean suggests quant clipping. Did we change final layer scaling during PTQ?
alex: PTQ config used clip_at=2.5, per_channel=false. For fp16/float baselines we didn't clip. Might be worth re-running with per_channel=true or higher clip.
sam: re-run plan: (1) int4-original-pcfg, (2) int4-perchannel-clip, (3) int4-higher-clip, (4) fp16 baseline. Compare NDCG/MRR and per-query variance.
sophie: I'll spin those runs overnight. For transparency I'll push results to the rerank-eval S3 bucket under `experiments/1764109876_int4_shortquery/`.

alex: one more ask — include a small human inspection sample (10 cases) with doc snippets so PMs can sanity-check relevance flips.
maria: also include tokenizer boundaries for those cases — sometimes subtoken splits influence very short queries.
sophie: noted. I'll add the human-sample CSV and a short Jupyter with visualization.

sam: if we can recover most of the delta with calibration, that's acceptable as an interim fix but we should file a PTQ follow-up to address the kernel/clip issue.
alex: agree. Also add a smoke tests in CI: run a small short-query NDCG probe after quant builds to catch regressions early.
sophie: will open a PR with the calibration script and CI probe once runs finish. Thanks all.

maria: thanks @sophie — ping us when the FP16 comparison is done.
sophie: will do :thumbsup:
